## What you should be able to do tonight

- Describe triple-barrier labelling, uniqueness weighting and meta-labelling from memory in three minutes total.
- State your frozen protocol without opening the file.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>35 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}

:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [15 min]{.task-min} Closed book: the three barriers and how they are set, the uniqueness calculation and what it corrects, the two-model structure of meta-labelling, and your protocol's five fields.

## Drill <span class='task-total'>interview thread</span>

Spaced repetition, not cramming. Every drill in the year is collected on the [drills page](../drills.qmd).

::: {.task-list .drill}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> Arithmetic, timed, thirty-first sitting. Ten two-digit multiplications and the sevenths.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> Regularisation out loud in ninety seconds: what ridge does to correlated predictors, what lasso does differently, and what the penalty is actually buying you in terms of bias and variance. Then the question they follow with: how would you choose the penalty when your folds are not independent?
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> A Python problem at second-round difficulty: implement a function that, given a list of (timestamp, price) ticks and a window in seconds, returns the rolling maximum efficiently. The naive version is quadratic; write the linear one with a deque and say why it is linear.
:::
:::
